# Product and experience: build rules

Apply these rules while you build. Domains or criteria whose `applies_if` flags are false in `.quality/project.json` do not apply to this project. Before you call a task done, check your work against the criteria of the domains you touched: each one must be true and verifiable.

If a stack module of Shipwright is installed (sw-nextjs, sw-node-api, sw-vps, sw-expo, sw-capacitor, sw-tauri, sw-electron), its rules skill adds stack-specific rules on top of these.

## Product (PRD)

Usefulness and promise: who the project serves, what problem it solves, what it promises.

Rules:

- Write the promise in one sentence (for whom, which problem, which outcome) before any code, in .quality/project.json.
- List what the project will not do (out of scope) to avoid useless features.
- Every feature must serve the promise; otherwise it leaves the scope.

Done means:

- [major] PRD-01: The promise is written in one sentence and up to date. Check: Promise present and consistent in .quality/project.json.
- [major] PRD-02: The first screen says what the product does and for whom, without jargon (only if: has_ui). Check: Read the home or entry screen: would a stranger get it in 5 seconds?
- [major] PRD-03: The main action is obvious and reachable on arrival (only if: has_ui). Check: One visible primary call to action on the entry screen.
- [minor] PRD-04: Every shipped feature serves the promise. Check: Compare the feature list with the promise and the out-of-scope list.
- [minor] PRD-05: A success metric is defined and measurable. Check: One metric (sign-ups, games played, sales…) and where it is measured.

## Features (FEA)

Complete behaviour: every announced feature works end to end.

Rules:

- Write a short spec per feature with acceptance criteria before coding.
- A feature is done only when its full flow has been run, not just compiled.
- No button, link or menu leading to a missing feature.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] FEA-01: No main flow is broken. Check: flows.json: each key task played to its expected result on phone and desktop; without declared flows, e2e tests or a manual run, saying so.
- [major] FEA-02: No dead link, inert button or visible 'coming soon' page. Check: Browse the UI and search for empty hrefs, empty onClick handlers, visible TODOs.
- [major] FEA-03: Every feature has written acceptance criteria that are met. Check: Specs present (docs/specs or tickets) and checked.
- [minor] FEA-04: No dead code or half-wired feature. Check: Search for unused exports, orphan routes, forgotten feature flags.

## UX (UX)

Smooth flows, explicit empty states and errors.

Applies when: The project has a user interface.

Rules:

- Every screen that shows data has 4 states: loading, empty, error, filled.
- An empty state explains the situation and offers the next action.
- An error message says what happened and how to recover, without raw technical codes.
- Any action over one second shows feedback; any destructive action asks for confirmation or can be undone.
- Forms keep the input on error and show the error next to the field.

Done means:

- [major] UX-01: Every data screen handles loading, empty, error and filled. Check: Read each data-loading component; simulate an empty list and a failing API; look at the filled state on the flow screenshots, not only the empty screen.
- [major] UX-02: Errors are explicit and offer a way out. Check: No bare 'Something went wrong', no raw technical message shown.
- [major] UX-03: Destructive actions are confirmed or undoable. Check: Delete, cancel, reset: confirmation or undo available.
- [major] UX-04: Forms validate inline and keep the input. Check: Submit an invalid form: errors next to fields, input kept.
- [minor] UX-05: Visual feedback on any action over one second. Check: Buttons show loading and are disabled while sending (no double submit).
- [minor] UX-06: Predictable navigation: back button, deep links, helpful 404. Check: Test the back button, open an inner URL directly, visit a missing URL.

## Content (CNT)

Clarity, accuracy and spelling of the text.

Applies when: The project has a user interface.

Rules:

- Write short, concrete sentences in the user's vocabulary, not the code's.
- No filler text (lorem ipsum, 'Your title here') or invented figures in production.
- One tone and one name for each thing across the whole project.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] CNT-01: No filler text or fake content in production. Check: Search for lorem ipsum, TODO, 'placeholder', fake testimonials, unsourced figures.
- [major] CNT-02: Correct spelling and grammar in every language. Check: Spell checker on copy and translation files.
- [major] CNT-03: Displayed information is accurate (prices, delays, features). Check: Compare the site's claims with actual behaviour and configuration.
- [minor] CNT-04: Consistent terminology and tone everywhere. Check: Same word for the same thing, consistent level of formality.
- [minor] CNT-05: No missing translation key or untranslated text (only if: multilingual). Check: Diff locale files; search for hard-coded strings in components.

## Support (SUP)

Help and problem resolution for users.

Rules:

- Provide a visible contact channel and a stated response time.
- Important error messages give an ID the user can send to support.
- Write an FAQ or help page from questions actually asked.

Done means:

- [major] SUP-01: A contact channel is reachable from every page. Check: Contact or help link in the footer or menu.
- [minor] SUP-02: Server errors show a reference ID linked to the logs (only if: has_backend). Check: Trigger a 500: an ID is shown and found in the logs.
- [minor] SUP-03: Common problems have a self-service fix (only if: has_auth). Check: Password reset, resend confirmation email, account deletion possible without contacting support.
- [minor] SUP-04: A help page or FAQ covers frequent questions. Check: Help page present and relevant.
